ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18467, as amended, the Specified Financial Information Act), Articles 2(1)(b), 5(2), 7, 13 and 25; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 19055, as amended); Commercial Act (Act No. 17905, as amended), Articles 316, 335 and 369-373; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 19544) and its Enforcement Decree; Financial Services Commission Public Announcement No. 2023-19 on Customer and Beneficial Owner Identification; FATF Recommendation 24 as incorporated into the KoFIU examination manual.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Parent Entity or Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National companies registrar or commercial registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive. (A) Hague Apostille path for a document issued in an Apostille Convention state: notarize if the state requires it, then have the competent authority of that state (Secretary of State, Department of State, or Ministry of Foreign Affairs) issue an Apostille; present the apostilled original directly to the Korean Registry or company counsel; do not visit a Korean Consulate. (B) Consular Legalization path for a document issued in a non-Convention state: notarize if required, authenticate at the state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate in that state; the Korean Consular Officer certifies the signature and seal; do not issue or attach an Apostille and never sequence the two paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence) of the Ultimate Parent Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of companies or tax authority in the foreign entity domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive. (A) Hague Apostille path: obtain the Certificate of Good Standing, notarize if required, then obtain an Apostille from the competent authority of the issuing jurisdiction and use the apostilled original in Korea; Korean consular legalization is not required. (B) Consular Legalization path: for a non-Apostille state, have the certificate authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate; never add an Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing local incorporators, representative and AML filing agents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate shareholder, notarized in the issuing jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive. If the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, execute the resolution, notarize the board signatures, and obtain an Apostille for presentation in Korea. If the issuing jurisdiction is not a member, execute and notarize the resolution, authenticate it through the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then obtain consular legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate. A Korean translation by a licensed translator must accompany either path. The two paths are parallel and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Certified Charter of the Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate secretary of the foreign shareholder with authority to certify constituent instruments
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive. For Apostille states, a certified registry extract is apostilled by the competent national authority and submitted with the Korean registration filing; no Korean consular action is required. For non-Apostille states, the certified extract is authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the Korean consular post. Do not combine an Apostille with consular legalization on the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Foreign Entity's Operating Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank where the foreign parent maintains its principal operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive. For Apostille Convention jurisdictions, the bank letter must be signed by an authorized bank officer, notarized as required, and then covered by an Apostille issued by the competent authority of that jurisdiction. For non-Convention jurisdictions, the notarized bank letter must be authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. The bank letter must be dated within 90 days and must verify account status, relationship length, and the absence of adverse conduct; it cannot be replaced by a customer self-declaration.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, UBOs at a direct or indirect ownership threshold of at least 25%, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and beneficial controllers must be screened continuously against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN/SSI lists including Korea-specific Executive Orders 13570, 13722 and 13810, EU consolidated sanctions lists, UK OFSI consolidated measures, and Korean FIU and Financial Services Commission high-risk jurisdiction notices. PEP screening covers domestic and foreign heads of state, senior officials, National Assembly members, and their immediate family and close associates. Positive hits require escalation to the AML compliance officer, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth substantiation, and, if suspicion is confirmed, a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU within 24 hours. Evidence to be retained includes full legal names, aliases, dates of birth, passport numbers, nationalities, addresses, and relationship diagrams.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO) - company name search and corporate registration module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean statute requires a Chusik Hoesa to have a corporate name in Hangul; the name must identify the entity as a stock company and must not be confusingly identical to an existing registered name. The registry applies a four-tier review: (i) the business purpose in the Articles of Association must support the name, (ii) the distinctive component must be distinguishable in the Korean alphabet, (iii) the corporate form suffix must appear in the Korean statutory form, and (iv) any English or foreign-language name is permitted only as a commercial alias, not as the legal registered name. Phonetic transliteration of a foreign corporate shareholder or brand into Hangul is acceptable, but the passport-order romanized name of a non-resident UBO must also be disclosed for foreign-exchange and AML reporting.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension exists for a rejected name; if the internal 30-day validity lapses, a new name search must be run. Where a registration officer rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written appeal with the competent District Court of the company seat within two weeks of receiving the rejection notice. The appeal must state the registry file number, the statutory basis for the proposed name, and evidence of distinguishability, such as prior search results, trademark registrations, or ministerial approvals for sensitive tokens. The District Court reviews the rejection on the papers and may overturn the registry decision. If the appeal is dismissed, an immediate appeal to the Supreme Court is available within two weeks only on a question of law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A professional virtual office with a physical desk, meeting room, mail handling, and signage is initially tolerably acceptable for registration of a low-risk email newsletter infrastructure company. However, the National Tax Service and Korean banks will reject a pure commercial mailbox or virtual address that lacks any physical presence. The registered office must support VAT invoice registration, bank account opening, foreign-exchange reporting, and service of process. The virtual office agreement must include a notarized lease or occupancy contract in the company name, a local contact person, and the ability to receive and store corporate records. A mailbox-only arrangement is not permissible and will trigger bank rejection and tax deregistration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk is quantified as low to moderate: approximately 10-15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months for a standard low-risk SaaS entity, rising to 25-30% if VAT refunds are large, invoices are issued from an undisclosed location, no employee is present, or the registered address does not match operating activity. Checklist: (1) exterior and interior company signage, (2) notarized lease or occupancy agreement in the company name, (3) utility or maintenance bills in the company name, (4) tax invoice issuing records tied to the registered address, (5) production servers or email infrastructure access available at the address, (6) local director or manager available for interview, and (7) accounting records physically or electronically accessible in Korea.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part IV on Chusik Hoesa or Stock Corporation, particularly Articles 288, 289, 291, 295, 299, 302, 389 and 393
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registration Division of the Republic of Korea, under the Supreme Court Registry Office, having jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Division)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation under Article 302 of the Korean Commercial Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Chusik Hoesa under current Korean law, and no blocked escrow account is statutorily mandated. However, the total par value of all issued shares must be fully paid in cash before incorporation registration is filed, and a bank-issued capital deposit certificate evidencing such payment must be submitted to the District Court Registry. The funds may not be withdrawn for business use until registration is complete. The official filing fee includes a court registration fee of approximately KRW 40,000 plus registration tax at 0.4 percent of stated capital and a local education surcharge equal to 20 percent of the registration tax.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA. RESOLUTION NO. [2025]-[001]. WHEREAS the inaugural general meeting of shareholders of the Company was duly convened and the directors of the Company were validly elected; and WHEREAS the board of directors is authorized by Article 393 of the Korean Commercial Act and by the Company's Articles of Incorporation to determine the administration of the Company and to supervise its business; NOW, THEREFORE, the board of directors, with all directors present and waiving formal notice of the meeting, acting unanimously and in accordance with the Company's charter, hereby adopts the following resolutions. 1. CONFIRMATION OF SHARE SUBSCRIPTION AND PAID-IN CAPITAL. The board confirms that the total issued share capital of the Company consisting of [number] ordinary shares with a par value of [amount] Korean won per share has been validly subscribed and fully paid in cash by the shareholders named in the subscription list. The certificate of capital deposit issued by [name of bank] is hereby approved and ordered to be retained in the corporate books, and the representative director is directed to complete the incorporation registration and to issue share certificates after registration. 2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The board adopts [full address], Republic of Korea, as the Company's registered office and principal place of business. The representative director is authorized to sign the lease, pay deposits and rent, procure utility accounts, and file all required statutory and tax notices with the local government and the District Court Registration Division. 3. BANKING AND CORPORATE MANDATE. The board designates [name of bank], [branch], as the Company's principal depositary and authorizes the opening of corporate demand-deposit accounts, foreign-currency accounts, checks, and electronic banking services. The representative director and one additional designated director, acting jointly for amounts above [threshold], and singly for ordinary operating amounts, shall be the bank's authorized signatories. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The board appoints [name] as Representative Director, [name] as Director, and [name] as Auditor where required by law. The Representative Director is authorized to execute all incorporation applications, appoint legal counsel, and submit this Resolution to the District Court Registration Division. 5. COMPLIANCE AND LICENSING. The board finds that the Company's business is a pure digital email newsletter infrastructure service under ISIC 6201 and that no industrial manufacturing or environmental operating permit is applicable, but directs management to complete business registration with the National Tax Service and to comply with applicable data protection duties under the Personal Information Protection Act. 6. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION AND EFFECTIVE DATE. All prior inconsistent instructions by promoters are revoked and superseded. These resolutions shall be effective upon adoption and remain in full force until amended or revoked by a subsequent board resolution. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, each director has executed this Resolution on [date] at [place].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public qualified under the Korean Notary Act in the jurisdiction of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must prepare Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in strict compliance with Articles 289 and 291 of the Korean Commercial Act. The document must state the corporate name, business object, authorized capital, class and par value of shares, number of issued shares, location of the registered office, names of promoters, method of announcement, and provisions concerning directors and auditor. Each promoter must personally sign and affix his or her seal or execute an electronic signature before the notary; if a promoter acts through counsel, a duly authenticated power of attorney and identification must be presented. The notary certifies the articles, and the notarized version becomes the definitive charter for registration. Before finalization, a name availability search should be completed through the Supreme Court corporate registration index to avoid identical or deceptively similar corporate names.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Promoter identification documents or passports
Corporate name availability search result
Power of attorney if executed by counsel
Personal seal certificates and proposed corporate seal imprint
Legal opinion on permitted business objects for ISIC 6201 email infrastructure services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification or the application is returned as defective, the promoters must amend the offending provisions, re-execute the Articles before the notary, and obtain a new notarial certificate. A corporate name conflict requires selection of a new name and resubmission of the name search certificate; substantive omissions in the objects clause must be corrected and re-notarized before any further filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Payment and Bank Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank authorized by the Financial Services Commission to accept Korean won and foreign currency deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after notarization, each subscriber must pay the full issue price of subscribed shares into a temporary bank account opened in the name of the corporation under formation. The bank issues a capital deposit certificate evidencing the payment, which is the conclusive proof of paid-in capital required by the District Court Registration Division. For non-resident investors, the remittance must comply with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and be reported through the receiving foreign exchange bank. Funds must remain deposited and may not be withdrawn before the incorporation registration is completed. No escrow account is required by law, but all bank records must match the number of shares, par value, subscriber names, and total amount specified in the Articles of Incorporation and subscription lists.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscriber identification documents or passports
Share subscription forms
Capital deposit certificate issued by the bank
Foreign exchange remittance and reporting documents for non-resident shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries beneficial ownership or source of funds, the promoters should provide the subscription list, passport or corporate identification, and a source-of-funds declaration. If the capital deposit certificate contains any discrepancy, the bank must amend and reissue it before the registration filing is submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Inaugural General Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Promoters, newly elected directors, auditor, and formation legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must convene an inaugural general meeting after the capital deposit is completed and before the incorporation application is submitted. At that meeting, the promoters approve the incorporation process, adopt the final Articles of Incorporation, confirm the paid-in capital, and elect the initial directors and, where required by law, the auditor. Immediately following the inaugural meeting, the directors must hold the first board of directors meeting and adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution confirming share subscription, appointing the representative director and other statutory officers, adopting the registered office, and authorizing banking operations. Complete minutes for both meetings must be prepared, signed, and retained. The minutes and the First Board Resolution are essential registry exhibits and must reflect the actual dates, attendance, quorum, and unanimous approvals.
required_dossiers: Notice or waiver of notice of the inaugural general meeting
Share subscription list and capital deposit certificate
Minutes of the inaugural general meeting
Minutes of the first board of directors meeting together with the pro-forma First Board Resolution
Consents and acceptance of office by directors and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If meeting procedures are challenged or found defective, the cure is to convene an adjourned or new meeting, give proper notice, obtain unanimous written consent from all shareholders and directors, or correct proxy and acceptance instruments before resubmission to the registration authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registration Division of the Republic of Korea having jurisdiction over the registered office, supervised by the Supreme Court of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory period following the inaugural general meeting, the representative director or authorized formation attorney must file the application for incorporation registration with the competent District Court Registration Division. The submission must include the prescribed registration application form, notarized Articles, capital deposit certificate, subscription forms, minutes of the inaugural general meeting and first board meeting, directors' and auditor's statements of acceptance, the registered-office lease or site-use consent, corporate seal card, and proof of payment of registration tax and local education surcharge. The registry will examine the file for legal compliance and, if approved, issue the corporate registration certificate and assign the corporate registration number. Electronic filing through the Supreme Court's registration information system may be used in place of in-person filing where available.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate
Minutes of the inaugural general meeting
Minutes of the first board of directors meeting and First Board Resolution
Director and auditor acceptance statements
Registered-office lease agreement or building owner's use consent
Corporate seal card and representative identification
Receipt for registration tax and local education surcharge
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction instruction or suspends the application, the representative director or counsel must remedy the specified deficiency within the registry's stated deadline, resubmit the corrected documents, and pay any additional filing charge. If the registered office consent is insufficient, obtain and file a fresh owner consent; if officer eligibility is questioned, replace the officer and file an amended board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service, District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office, with filing available directly or through the HomeTax online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the corporate registration certificate, the representative director must apply for business registration with the competent District Tax Office under the Value-Added Tax Act and Corporation Tax Act. The application requests assignment of a business registration number, confirmation of tax invoice issuance, corporate income tax registration, and employment withholding registration. The business type must be stated as software development, cloud-hosted communications infrastructure, and email newsletter services corresponding to ISIC 6201 and the Korean Standard Industrial Classification equivalent. The tax office will verify the registered office address, the lessee status, and the representative's identification. Because the enterprise is a pure digital email infrastructure service, no separate industrial or manufacturing license is required from the National Tax Service. After NTS registration, the company should activate its operating bank accounts and obtain an issued corporate seal certificate for banking and commercial contracts.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate issued by the District Court Registration Division
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form
Registered-office lease agreement or ownership evidence
Representative director's identification
Bank capital deposit certificate and corporate seal card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service issues a correction notice or requests additional evidence, the representative director must respond within the notice period, provide the lease agreement and registration certificate, and correct any inconsistency in the business code or registered address. If the tax office rejects the classification, the applicant should align the Korean Standard Industrial Classification code with ISIC 6201 and resubmit with an explanation of the SaaS email infrastructure activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the enterprise is a pure digital email newsletter infrastructure and hosting platform under ISIC 6201, not a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation within ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx or 52xx.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license, factory permit, assembly permit, or warehousing permit is required for the email API and newsletter hosting platform.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea - Not Applicable for a pure digital service activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity creates no physical discharge unit, manufacturing plant, fuel combustion facility, or hazardous waste storage, and therefore requires no Environmental Impact Assessment, Environmental Registration, or pre-approval.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, VOC emission units, noise threshold, or hazardous waste generation arise from the email newsletter infrastructure service. The company's servers and data infrastructure are expected to be hosted by third-party cloud providers and are not owned physical facilities. General office waste must be disposed of under municipal solid waste rules, and end-of-life office electronics should be transferred to licensed e-waste recyclers where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to a factory-level Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or special industrial workplace safety approval because no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility is established. General workplace duties under the Korean Occupational Safety and Health Act remain applicable to the office environment, and the building owner must maintain fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and civil defense fire safety systems. The company should maintain basic fire extinguishers, employee safety training records, and an emergency evacuation plan for its office employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the Hometax electronic tax portal at www.hometax.go.kr; cross-border trade and customs processing are handled by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic customs portal at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a resident Chusik Hoesa, the company must commence business registration within 20 days of business opening by filing an application with the competent district tax office through Hometax. The statutory tax identifier is the 10-digit Korean Business Registration Number (BRN) issued under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes. The required documentary bundle includes the certificate of incorporation, certified corporate articles, lease or ownership evidence for the registered business premises, nominee or representative director identification, and where applicable the foreign investment registration certificate under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Upon NTS acceptance, Hometax issues the BRN, which serves as the company's unified tax account for corporate income tax, VAT, withholding, and customs-adjacent tax filings. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean domestic place of business, the entity must appoint a Korean tax representative, register through Hometax using an accredited public-joint certificate, and submit the foreign certificate of incorporation, a foreign business license or equivalent registration extract, a board resolution appointing the tax representative, a power of attorney, and a declaration confirming the absence of a Korean domestic business place. NTS will then issue a foreign corporation BRN or equivalent Korean taxpayer identifier enabling VAT return filing, electronic tax invoice issuance, and payment of Korean VAT where the foreign entity supplies electronic services or other taxable Korean-source services. The entire registration flow is completed electronically; no physical visit is generally required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification. The Republic of Korea does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid entity election under its domestic tax law; a Chusik Hoesa is per se a corporate income taxpayer taxed at the entity level on worldwide income. The only relevant elective regimes are group consolation and special tax incentive elections, none of which alter the entity classification or VAT registration framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover threshold for mandatory registration: any business making taxable supplies of goods or services in Korea, including a Chusik Hoesa operating an email newsletter hosting platform, must register for VAT from its first taxable supply. A simplified taxpayer regime exists for small suppliers with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000, but such taxpayers remain legally required to hold a Business Registration Number and issue VAT invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates electronic tax invoices for business-to-business taxable supplies. Every registered business must issue a Korean tax invoice through the NTS Hometax Electronic Tax Invoice system, either directly through Hometax or via an NTS-certified electronic tax invoice service provider. Invoice data must be transmitted to NTS in the form and within the timeline prescribed by the NTS Commissioner. NTS does not pre-approve or digitally stamp individual invoices before issuance; anti-fraud integrity is achieved through mandatory transmission of e-invoice data into the Hometax database, real-time cross-matching against filed VAT returns and buyer credit claims, risk-based audit analytics, and statutory penalty surcharges for false or omitted invoice data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act when the goods are exported and supported by customs export documentation. The supply of services to foreign customers is also zero-rated when the recipient is a non-resident and the service is deemed supplied or consumed outside Korea under the place-of-supply rules. For the email infrastructure SaaS scope, bulk transactional email, newsletter hosting, API delivery, and related digital platform services supplied to foreign subscribers or foreign businesses without a Korean place of business and with actual use outside Korea meet the statutory offshore service criterion. The supplier may claim full input VAT credit on costs directly attributable to zero-rated export activities and may file a VAT refund when input VAT exceeds output VAT; the refund is subject to NTS documentation review.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korean Customs Export Declaration filed through the UNI-PASS system for physical goods movements
Bill of Lading or airway bill evidencing physical export to a foreign destination

For pure digital services: signed service agreement with the foreign customer, monthly usage and performance records generated by the email infrastructure platform, foreign-currency service invoice addressed to the non-resident customer, and bank records showing receipt of the export consideration
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank-issued foreign exchange receipt confirming receipt from overseas in KRW or foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly review zero-rating evidence. If the claimed export is not substantiated by customs clearance, foreign consumption evidence, or foreign exchange repatriation within the statutory 180-day deadline, the 0% rate is denied retroactively, the VAT becomes payable with statutory interest, and the related input VAT credits are clawed back. Additional penalty surcharges are imposed under the Value-Added Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes, including penalties for false tax invoices, unreported or underreported VAT, failure to transmit e-invoice data, and fraudulent refund claims. Fraudulent or wilful zero-rating claims may constitute criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and can result in imprisonment, fines, publication of taxpayer information, and extended statute-of-limitations assessment periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) with the Ministry of Economy and Finance, operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised but supervised foreign exchange regime. Current account transactions are generally free: legitimate cross-border payments for trade, software subscriptions, cloud services and newsletter infrastructure fees can be settled in foreign currency or KRW through a designated Foreign Exchange Bank (FX Bank). The old fixed export surrender ratio has been replaced by a monitoring-based system; proceeds must be received through an FX Bank and reported, but the bank may hold them in a retained foreign currency account or convert to KRW at market rates. Capital account items are subject to a positive-list declaration regime: non-resident equity subscription, inter-company financing and profit remittance require advance filing under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Dividend repatriation from a Chusik Hoesa is permitted after capital verification, audited financial statements and withholding tax payment, but the bank will require the final shareholders resolution and confirmation of no unresolved tax liabilities. A foreign investor must complete a foreign investment report before inward remittance; the KRW conversion is then recorded and monitored. Service revenue from email newsletter platform operations is transactionally convertible, but any suspicious or unsubstantiated flow will be blocked by bank compliance committees under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information. Overall, the KRW is largely convertible on current account and selectively convertible on capital account, with procedural rather than absolute restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion ratio applies; under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export and service proceeds must be received through a domestic FX bank within one year of the transaction unless extended. The exporter or service provider reports the withdrawal and can either keep foreign currency in an FX account or sell it to the bank. Non-repatriation within the statutory timeline requires prior approval and triggers a report to the Bank of Korea.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-inadmissible as a primary treasury rail. Non-bank offshore EMIs are not licensed foreign exchange banks under Korean law and cannot perform foreign investment capital verification or issue the certificate of receipt needed for the Foreign Investment Promotion Act report. An EMI may only be used for outward collection from SaaS customers if integrated through a licensed international gateway, but all corporate liquidity, statutory capital and tax settlement must remain in a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean banks generally accept non-face-to-face onboarding for locally incorporated companies using a certified corporate digital certificate and representative identification, but for non-resident directors or foreign-controlled Chusik Hoesa the compliance committee normally requires either an in-branch interview of at least one statutory director or a notarised and consular-certified power of attorney authorising a local representative to attend in person. Remote video interviews are accepted by some banks where the UBO has existing relationship and complete apostilled corporate pack is provided.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain contains a foreign holding company or nominee-like ownership structure without transparent economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a signed group ownership chart, certificate of incorporation and articles of association of each UBO entity, apostilled passports and proof of residential address for every natural person holding 10% or more, sworn beneficial ownership declaration, and audited financial statements for the immediate parent if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial equity capital source is not evidenced by an institutionally verifiable trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the investor's 12-month bank statements, source-of-wealth file (asset sale agreements, share trading statements, tax returns), a notarised gift/loan agreement if applicable, and a written confirmation that no third-party nominee funding is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The email newsletter platform is perceived as having anonymous recipients or exposure to international sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Acceptable Use Policy, opt-in and consent audit logs, subscriber country distribution report, automated sanctions/OFAC/UN screening records, data centre and infrastructure contracts, and a legal opinion confirming data protection and anti-spam compliance in South Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No demonstrable physical business presence in the jurisdiction of incorporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply a registered office lease or virtual office agreement with a licensed provider, local management and payroll records, VAT/tax registration certificates, insurance policies, and contracts with domestic email infrastructure or security vendors proving operational substance in South Korea.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: A non-resident shareholder wires equity funds from an overseas account to the designated Capital Escrow Account at a Tier-1 Korean FX bank using SWIFT MT103, quoting purpose code for foreign direct investment and the company's foreign investment report registration number. Before remittance, the entity files a foreign investment report with the bank or KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Upon receipt the bank issues a certificate of receipt; the company submits the certificate, board resolution and shareholder ledger to complete capital verification. Funds are convertible to KRW at market rates or retained as foreign currency, and the bank records the transaction for the Foreign Exchange Information System.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recurring international infrastructure costs, licensing fees and vendor payments are settled by SWIFT MT103 with itemised invoices and underlying contracts. High-value or order-based equipment and outsourced service arrangements may be covered by an irrevocable commercial letter of credit opened by the Korean bank using MT700, while documentary collections are less suitable for subscription email infrastructure and should be used only where the vendor is treaty-based and requires bank verification of shipping documents. All outbound payments must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code framework and supported by board-approved disbursement minutes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable Korean Won/USD forward contracts for actual commercial exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted through a Korean FX bank for hedging offshore funding positions
Cross-currency interest rate swaps on bank-approved medium-term foreign debt
Limited FX options with documented underlying exposure and confirmed no speculative intent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return including official financial statements and tax base schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end, i.e., the last day of the third month after the fiscal-year close; an extension of one month to April 30 is available when the return is prepared and certified by a licensed Korean tax accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers NTS assessed assessment plus 20% additional tax on unreported tax liability (40% if fraudulent); unpaid corporate tax accrues late-payment interest at 0.022% per day, approximately 8.03% per annum; chronic non-filing and non-payment can result in seizure of corporate assets, NTS closure of the business place, revocation of the business registration certificate, and court-ordered dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surtax on national corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent metropolitan city or provincial local government tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing and payment due on the same statutory due date as the national corporate income tax return, generally March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end, with the same one-month extension for tax-agent-certified returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid local corporate income tax attracts local administrative surcharges, late-filing penalties, and daily late-payment interest at 0.022%; prolonged non-payment enables local government enforced collection, asset attachment, and business registration cancellation coordination with the NTS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit engagement, auditor appointment, and filing of audited financial statements with the financial regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART, with audit report also delivered to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For companies meeting statutory audit thresholds, the external auditor must be appointed before the relevant fiscal year-end; audited financial statements must be approved at the annual shareholders meeting within three months after fiscal year-end; the audited statements must be filed with FSS through DART within 14 days of shareholders meeting approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-appointment of a required external auditor or failure to file audited financial statements with FSS constitutes an enforcement event under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, subjecting the company and directors to administrative sanctions, regulatory admonitions, monetary penalties, audit-committee restrictions, and possible referral to NTS for revised tax assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting, approval of annual financial statements, and retention of statutory corporate minutes and books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records maintained at the registered office; not filed with a government register unless the company is an external-audit target
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual general meeting must be held within three months after the end of each fiscal year, so for a December 31 fiscal year-end the meeting must occur by March 31; approved financial statements and related schedules must be kept at the head office for at least seven years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual general meeting within the statutory window does not itself trigger government strike-off, but it exposes directors to personal liability, invalidates procedural steps such as dividend distributions, allows shareholders to petition the court for appointment of an inspector or for dissolution in cases of deadlock, and constitutes a serious governance breach for external-audit companies subject to FSS inspection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment change notification and foreign ownership record update for foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance and Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency through a designated foreign-exchange bank in Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual UBO return is required; however, if the company is a foreign-invested company with foreign ownership of at least 10% and an investment amount of at least KRW 100 million, any share transfer, capital increase, capital reduction, or change in foreign ownership percentage must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the required foreign investment change notification within the 30-day window may result in administrative fines, loss of certain foreign-invested company benefits, delay or refusal of foreign exchange bank approvals, and reputational obstacles in future regulatory filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax quarterly returns and tax invoice reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Four annual statutory filing windows: Q1 (January-March) due April 25; Q2 (April-June) due July 25; Q3 (July-September) due October 25; Q4 (October-December) due January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted VAT is subject to an additional tax of 10% of the unreported amount, plus daily late-payment interest at 0.022%; failure to issue electronic tax invoices may trigger an additional tax up to 1% of the supply value; persistent VAT default may trigger NTS compulsory collection, business closure, and registration revocation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, an independent certified CPA audit is legally mandatory for: (1) all listed companies in South Korea; (2) non-listed stock companies whose total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 8.6 million; (3) financial institutions, securities firms, insurance companies, and other capital-market authorization holders; (4) companies designated by the Securities and Futures Commission because of public-interest scale or systemic relevance; and (5) subsidiaries or parent companies integrated into an audited consolidated group that is itself subject to external audit. Relevant quantitative proxies used in the Korean statutory audit framework include total liabilities of KRW 7 billion or more, annual turnover of KRW 20 billion or more, and a workforce above approximately 100 full-time employees, particularly when assessing group consolidated scale or small-enterprise simplified audit eligibility; the bright-line general rule remains total assets of KRW 12 billion or more. Companies below the mandatory audit threshold may still be voluntarily audited if shareholders, lenders, or investors require it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS, the Korean adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards, is mandatory for listed companies and for external-audit target companies; non-listed companies not subject to mandatory external audit may prepare their financial statements under Korean GAAP adapted for non-public companies, including the Korean SME Accounting Standards while still maintaining compatibility with the Commercial Act and the Corporate Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate a separate annual UBO confirmation filing for an ordinary private Chusik Hoesa. The company is required to maintain and update its Register of Shareholders at the registered office, and a shareholder is recognized as a member only after transfer is recorded in that register. Any share transfer, issuance of new shares, or cancellation of shares must be reflected in the register of shareholders without undue delay currently before the record date for any general meeting. For a foreign-invested company under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, where a foreign investor holds 10% or more of shares with an aggregate investment of KRW 100 million or more, any change in that foreign holding ratio, capital amount, or share transfer must be filed with a designated foreign-exchange bank or KOTRA within 30 days of the occurrence. For AML purposes, the company is not itself a financial institution, but the Korean bank and payment processors handling Stripe payouts and credit-card settlements will conduct standard customer due diligence; the company must respond to lawful requests for controlling-party and shareholder information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders maintained at the registered office
Register of Directors and executive officers maintained in conjunction with commercial registry filings
Register of Charges, Mortgages, and security interests over company assets where encumbrances exist
Minute book of shareholders general meetings
Minute book of board of directors meetings
Corporate accounting books, ledgers, and retained financial statements available for inspection

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - USD 4,500 per year for a Seoul or Incheon registered-office address, commercial registration maintenance, and corporate secretarial retainer with a local law firm or corporate service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 25,000 per year for a small-to-mid-market Korean statutory audit engagement, including CPA certification, financial statement preparation oversight, and audit report filing where applicable; fees increase for consolidated groups, listed companies, or transactions requiring complex revenue recognition

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national top CIT bracket plus 10% local income tax surtax (aggregate top rate 26.4%); progressive lower brackets apply up to KRW 200m (10%), KRW 20bn (20%), and KRW 300bn (22%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea has no general patent-box regime; statutory incentives include R&D tax credits for qualifying research and personnel expenses, investment tax credits, foreign-invested enterprise tax reductions, Free Economic Zone CIT reductions of up to 50-100% for 5-10 years, and SME/Green-New-Deal credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form 51 (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return) filed electronically through HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) or approved NTS EDI software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim estimated corporate tax prepayment is due within two months after the first six months of the fiscal year (August 31 for calendar-year corporations).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year under Article 60 of the Corporate Income Tax Act (March 31 for calendar year-end); a one-month filing extension is available for corporations subject to external audit, and extensions must be applied through HomeTax before the original deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All revenue from email newsletter SaaS, bulk transactional email API fees, usage-based sending charges, and setup fees before VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A domestic Chusik Hoesa reports worldwide revenue. Invoices to non-resident customers are export VAT-exempt, but must be included in CIT gross revenue; convert foreign-currency receipts at the NTS-recognized rate and reconcile to Stripe Billing settlement reports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (Line 4) - Cost of Sales / Cloud Infrastructure Costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs for server hosting, email delivery infrastructure, bandwidth, subcontracting, and network security.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany cloud costs paid to foreign affiliates require arm's length documentation and reverse-charge VAT treatment; costs lacking Korean economic substance may be disallowed and recharacterized as constructive dividends to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (Line 11) - Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payroll, marketing, legal fees, software tools, office rent, and ordinary operating deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, support fees, and royalties paid to non-resident affiliates must satisfy the arm's length standard and be supported by e-invoices, signed contracts, and beneficial ownership statements; disallowed related-party expenses trigger under-reporting surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Line 16) - Taxable Income After Adjustments and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed after adding non-deductible expenses, applying tax-exempt income, and deducting carried-forward net operating losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not recognized on this line; declared or deemed dividends are not deductible. Loss carryforward of 15 years applies to losses incurred after 2019, while pre-2019 losses carry forward for 10 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 (Line 20) - Tax Credits and Foreign Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for Korean R&D credits, employment/investment tax credits, and foreign tax credits for taxes paid to foreign source jurisdictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding taxes suffered on overseas email-infrastructure income are creditable only by producing official foreign tax receipts and satisfying treaty residency requirements; treaty benefit claims require a valid Tax Residency Certificate from the foreign tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Headline national CIT computed on the final taxable income after credits, with local income tax surtax reported separately to the local government.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Chusik Hoesa is not relieved from non-resident dividend withholding by paying corporate tax; the board must separately file a withholding return and remit 22% aggregate WHT before any dividend remittance to foreign shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of unpaid corporate tax; under-reported income triggers 10% additional tax (20% if fraudulently concealed); daily late-payment interest accrues at approximately 0.022% per day (about 8.03% per annum). Criminal evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with fines up to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment up to three years, rising to five years for aggravated evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory dividend withholding tax for non-resident shareholders (20% national withholding under Article 98 of the Corporate Income Tax Act plus 2 percentage points from the 10% local income tax surcharge). Reduced treaty rates, generally 10% for qualifying substantial shareholders and 15% for portfolio shareholders under major Korean DTAs, apply only after treaty relief is approved.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must file the prescribed NTS Application for Tax Exemption/Reduction under Tax Treaties and a Beneficial Owner Statement before or on the payment date, together with a Tax Residency Certificate, proof of shareholding percentage and holding period, and evidence of substantive economic ownership; NTS may issue a reduced-withholding approval, and if over-withheld, a refund claim may be filed within three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest and royalty withholding rates are each 22% aggregate (20% national plus 2 percentage points local surtax). Under most Korean treaties, arm's length interest and royalties are commonly reduced to 10% or 5% depending on the counterparty; software/SaaS royalty characterization may be reclassified as business profits under newer DTAs, requiring a permanent-establishment analysis before treaty relief is claimed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is required when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion in the fiscal year; Master File is required when annual turnover exceeds KRW 100 billion; Country-by-Country Report is required for consolidated groups with total revenue of KRW 5 trillion or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation, but NTS applies the economic substance doctrine and substance-over-form principles; a Korean Chusik Hoesa must perform the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) with local employees, active management, office/network infrastructure, and strategic decision-making. Absent substance, profits may be recharacterized as distributions to non-residents, and the Korean CFC rules can attribute offshore passive income to controlling Korean shareholder-directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting email subscription and API usage revenue from Stripe settlement records, issuing fictitious cost invoices from shell contractors, or maintaining dual books to understate Korean CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, willful tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to three times the evaded tax; NTS also imposes a 20% fraudulent under-reporting surcharge and can suspend tax certificates and VAT e-invoice issuance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil when the Chusik Hoesa is used as a facade; the representative director becomes jointly and severally liable for unpaid CIT, personal assets are subject to seizure, travel bans are imposed through the National Tax Collection Act, and directors who signed false returns face criminal imprisonment up to three years, or five years in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Non-Compliance and Unlawful Profit Remittance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to non-resident shareholders or paying interest/royalties to foreign related parties without applying the 22% statutory Korean WHT, falsely claiming a tax treaty without a Tax Residency Certificate, or disguising dividends as email-infrastructure service fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is personally liable for the unwithheld tax, plus a withholding non-reporting surcharge of up to 20% and daily late-payment interest at 0.022% per day; deliberate non-withholding also constitutes a criminal tax collection offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the compliance officer are personally and jointly liable for unremitted withholding tax, deemed dividend taxes, and penalties; NTS can blacklist directors, order travel restrictions, seize personal and corporate accounts, and refer intentional false treaty claims for criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to three years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Shell Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the Korean entity as a low-margin routine service provider while shifting email newsletter platform IP and valuable intangible profits to a zero-tax foreign affiliate, charging non-arm's length cloud fees, or failing to prepare Local File, Master File, and OECD-consistent documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS re-determines taxable income on an arm's length basis under Article 4 of the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, disallows non-arm's length payments, imposes an under-reporting penalty of 10% (20% when concealed) with daily delinquency interest, and applies statutory TP documentation penalties for failure to attach the required files.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be assessed as secondary taxpayers under the Basic National Tax Act if corporate assets are insufficient; intentional TP manipulation exposes directors to personal civil restitution, travel bans and blacklisting, and criminal imprisonment up to three years for submitting false evidence during an NTS transfer-pricing audit.
